Chapter 5: Embracing Spirituality—Finding Strength and Meaning in the In-Between.
You know, for so many of us, those in-between times can feel like standing at a spiritual crossroads. The usual signposts—our relationships, our roles, even our daily routines—they’ve shifted or maybe disappeared altogether. What’s left behind? Sure, there can be a real sense of emptiness, but there’s also this incredible feeling of possibility. It’s in these quiet spaces that the big questions bubble up—questions about meaning, about purpose, and how we’re connected to something greater.
Imagine this: there’s a man who just lost his job and ended a long-term relationship. Suddenly, he’s adrift. The future he’d planned out? Gone. The present? Totally uncertain. In his search for comfort, he tried things he’d once brushed off—meditation, journaling, even peaceful walks out in nature. And slowly, he started to feel something shift. There was a presence, something beyond his own worries and fears. The meantime, he realized, wasn’t just about loss—it was a doorway to something deeper.
Spirituality in these in-between moments isn’t about following strict rules or clinging to old beliefs. It’s really about finding what nourishes your soul and brings you peace. For some, that’s prayer or joining a spiritual community. For others, it might be as simple as taking a few quiet moments, feeling grateful, or connecting with the natural world. The form doesn’t matter nearly as much as the intention—to listen, to trust, and to open yourself to something bigger than just you.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we lean on external things—relationships, achievements, our possessions—to feel safe and secure. But the meantime strips all that away. Suddenly, you’re left with just yourself. And while that might feel scary at first, it can actually be incredibly freeing. In that emptiness, there’s space for new insights, fresh dreams, and a deeper sense of belonging.
Take the story of a woman who was grieving the end of a close friendship. She started writing letters she never sent—pouring out her hopes, her fears, the regrets she carried. She trusted that someone, or maybe something, was listening. Over time, that writing became a kind of prayer. It helped her connect with her own heart, and with the mysterious flow of life itself.
Here’s something to really pay attention to—spirituality gives us perspective. The meantime, with all its uncertainty, starts to feel like just one part of a much bigger story. The pain and confusion? They’re not the end—they’re just a chapter in your journey of growth. Suddenly, even the toughest experiences seem to hold some meaning and value.
As you stick with your spiritual practices, the meantime shifts. It’s no longer just about waiting—it’s about becoming. You start to trust that life is unfolding exactly as it should, even when you can’t see what’s next. Your heart softens, your mind quiets, and hope begins to bloom again.
And in this open space, the seeds of new love start to grow—not just romantic love, but love for yourself, for others, even for the world around you. The meantime, once something you dreaded, becomes a sacred space of transformation. It’s where you let go of what’s old, welcome in what’s new, and let your soul get ready for whatever comes next.
